title: A test playbook ran against production
intro: A developer ran 'ansible-playbook reset-demo-data.yml' to reset the staging database. It printed 'changed' for db-01, the production database. The shop's product catalog is now the demo catalog. You need to know what happened, restore production, and stop this from recurring.

steps.prompt: Check which inventory Ansible uses when none is given on the command line: look at the ansible.cfg in the repo.
steps.hint: ansible.cfg in the current directory sets defaults.

steps.prompt: The default inventory is prod. Check which hosts reset-demo-data.yml targets.
steps.fake_output:
playbook: reset-demo-data.yml
  play #1 (db): Reset demo data	TAGS: []
    pattern: ['db']
    hosts (1):
      db-01

steps.prompt: The play targets the group 'db', which exists in both inventories. Restore production: find the most recent snapshot of db-01 from before the incident, in the restic repository.
The 10:00 hourly snapshot predates the 10:41 incident. Restore just the database dump from snapshot 5c4d3e2f into /tmp/restore.
steps.fake_output:
restoring <Snapshot 5c4d3e2f of [/etc /backup] at 2026-09-28 10:00:02> to /tmp/restore
Summary: Restored 1 files/dirs (2.4 GiB) in 0:21

steps.prompt: Restore only the catalog tables (products and categories) from the dump into the shop database, leaving orders placed since 10:00 untouched.
expected_commands: sudo -u postgres pg_restore -d shop --clean -t products -t categories /tmp/restore/backup/shop.dump
steps.fake_output: (no output: products and categories restored as of 10:00)
steps.hint: pg_restore -t <table> restores selected tables; --clean drops them first.

resolution: Nothing was 'wrong' with any single piece. The repo's ansible.cfg defaulted to the production inventory, both inventories had a group called 'db', the playbook had no guard, and the developer had production credentials. Ansible did exactly what it was told. Restoring only the affected tables from the 10:00 snapshot kept the orders placed since then; a full restore would have lost 41 minutes of real sales. That table-level restore was only possible because backups were custom-format dumps, taken hourly. Prevention, from strongest to weakest: (1) people shouldn't be able to reach production from a laptop at all; production runs go through CI with an approval; (2) no default inventory in ansible.cfg, so every run must name one explicitly; (3) destructive playbooks assert the environment ('assert: that: env == "staging"') and ask for confirmation (pause); (4) distinct group names or credentials per environment. Also write the blameless postmortem. The Writing Labs include one.
